title: Preemption fairness regression and eviction wave diagnostics
summary: Notes from initial on-call triage for a sudden cluster-wide spike in pod preemptions and correlated eviction waves in us-west-2. Suspected regression introduced by scheduler scoring plugin change deployed in the 2026-02-09 rollout. This doc captures observations, commands we ran, mitigation we applied, and proposed follow-ups.
symptoms: Between 03:15 and 03:40 UTC, multiple namespaces reported large numbers of Pending -> Evicted/Preempted events. Pod restart churn increased, user-reported 503s from inference endpoints, autoscaler oscillations triggered by rapid pod churn. Node available resources (Allocatable CPU/memory) did not show cluster-level shortage — rather, pods were being preempted out of nodes where they previously ran for days. Scheduler logs show increased Preemption decisions and score ties.
quick_timeline:
2026-02-09 22:30 PST: rolling deploy of scheduler v1.27-custom with new scoring plugin (strict-topology) to control bin-packing
2026-02-10 03:17 UTC: Pager triggered for increased pod restarts in us-west-2 prod cluster
03:20 UTC: SRE oncall (Priya) starts triage, confirms spike in Preemption events via kubectl and Grafana
03:28 UTC: Rolled back scheduler to previous version in control-plane for us-west-2 (partial)
03:40 UTC: Preemption rate drops, evictions stabilize; follow-up investigation started
commands_run:
kubectl get events --all-namespaces --field-selector reason=Preempted -o wide | head -n 200
kubectl describe node ip-10-0-4-23 | egrep -A4 'Non-terminated Pods'
journalctl -u kube-scheduler -o cat | sed -n '1,200p' | grep -i preempt
kubectl get pods -n prod -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,PRIORITY:.spec.priority,STATUS:.status.phase --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | tail -n 100
curl -sS "https://grafana.redwood.com/render/d-solo/cluster/scheduler-metrics?panelId=3&from=now-1h&to=now" -o scheduler-preemption.png
root_cause_hypotheses:
1) Scoring plugin change introduced different tie-breaking behavior that aggressively favors preempting medium-priority pods when topology-scores are tied.
2) A scheduling race under load increased scheduler latency causing stale scheduling decisions and duplicate preemption candidates.
3) Mistuned preemption cost heuristics in our custom scheduler fork (recent commit 4f3a9b) increased preemption score delta for low-memory nodes.
Evidence: timing correlates with scheduler rollout; logs show many preemption decisions with identical scores; rollback reduced rate.
mitigation_steps_taken:
1) Immediate rollback of scheduler binary in us-west-2 control plane partial rollout (~03:28 UTC).
2) Temporarily increased eviction gracePeriod for critical namespaces to reduce restart churn (patch applied to pod disruption budgets).
3) Added a temporary admission webhook block for best-effort pods in prod to avoid low-priority churn while we investigate.
Outcome: preemption rate dropped to baseline within ~12 minutes of rollback; user-facing errors decreased.
persistent_actions:
- Create a canary rollout plan for scheduler scoring plugin updates with traffic shaping and synthetic preemption checks.
- Add unit/integration test that simulates score ties and verifies deterministic tie-breaking consistent with prior behavior.
- Audit custom preemption heuristics in commit history and add guardrails (feature flag + kill switch).
- Add Grafana alert to detect preemption rate > 5/hr sustained for 5 minutes per region.
next_steps:
- Full postmortem to be written after deeper log correlation and scheduler trace capture (owner: Priya, due 2026-02-18).
- Reproduce locally: create a mini-cluster with our custom scheduler and run the synthetic workload that caused tie scores. (Ethan)
- Patch scheduler to preserve previous tie-break ordering or make tie-break explicit, then perform staged rollout with 1% canary. (Claire)
- Follow up with product teams about autoscaler backoff behavior to reduce oscillation during similar events.
notes_to_oncall: If you see a preemption spike: 1) check scheduler rollout history (kubectl -n kube-system rollout history deployment/kube-scheduler); 2) query recent scheduler logs for 'Preemption' and 'score tie' strings; 3) consider partial rollback of scheduler binary if correlating with deploy; 4) temporarily raise critical pod terminationGracePeriod and pause non-essential jobs; 5) ping eng-sre Slack #sre-oncall and cc @Priya and @Ethan. Include timestamps and sample pod names when filing a follow-up Linear ticket.
freeform_notes:
- Observed interesting pattern: many preempted pods shared same topologySpread constraints; scoring plugin was aggressively trying to satisfy topologies which produced more preemption candidates than before.
- Autoscaler amplified problem: nodes freed by preemptions triggered scale-down observations in ASG, which then forced additional re-scheduling and further churn.
- Consider adding a short cooldown on node-scale-down when preemption rate is high.
- Need to coordinate rollback/playbook with Platform team to avoid control-plane config drift in future deploys.
